vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: certcheck
Version: 2.0.0

The skill exhibits a significant discrepancy between its documentation and implementation. While SKILL.md describes a tool for SSL/TLS certificate analysis (commands like 'check' and 'expiry'), scripts/script.sh contains no networking or certificate logic; instead, it implements a generic logging system (commands like 'store', 'retrieve', 'audit') that simply appends input strings to local files in ~/.local/share/certcheck/. This misleading architecture is suspicious as it could trick an AI agent into saving sensitive information into local logs under the guise of security operations, though no evidence of automated data exfiltration or remote execution was found.

llm.summary: The skill's documentation promises an SSL/TLS certificate checker, but the included runtime script and SKILL.md disagree about commands and configuration and the script creates persistent logs in your home directory—these mismatches and unexplained behaviors merit caution and further review before installing.

dimensions.detail: The SKILL.md advertises commands like `check`, `expiry`, `chain`, and `batch` for inspecting certificates, but the bundled script's help text (and implemented commands shown) lists many unrelated operations (generate, store, retrieve, rotate, audit, policy, revoke, etc.). This divergence suggests the code may not implement the advertised cert-checking capability or includes extra functionality not disclosed in the description.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs users to set CERTCHECK_DIR to control data storage, and documents specific runtime commands that are missing or different in the script. The script writes to a persistent directory (~/.local/share/certcheck) and logs user inputs; this I/O behavior is not clearly described in SKILL.md and could capture arbitrary inputs. The instructions therefore do not align closely with what the runtime code actually does.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no install specification (instruction-only skill plus a script file), so nothing is downloaded or installed during registration. The script is included in the package; no external install URLs or package manager use were observed.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The registry metadata lists no required environment variables, yet SKILL.md documents a CERTCHECK_DIR env var to change the data directory. The script as shown ignores CERTCHECK_DIR and hardcodes DATA_DIR to $HOME/.local/share/certcheck. This mismatch is disproportionate and misleading: the skill will create and write files under the user's home without the declared configurable env var taking effect.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The script creates and writes multiple log files under ~/.local/share/certcheck and reads them for commands like search, stats, export, and status. It does not request elevated privileges nor set always:true, but it does persist user inputs locally. Persisting logs is reasonable for a tool that tracks activity, but because the script can store arbitrary input entries (store/retrieve/generate/etc.), it could inadvertently persist sensitive data—users should be aware of the storage location and contents.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Do not install this skill without additional review. Specific things to check before using: (1) Inspect the remainder of scripts/script.sh (the file was truncated in the preview) for any network calls (curl, wget, openssl s_client, nc, etc.) or commands that would send data off-host. (2) Verify whether the advertised commands (check, expiry, chain, batch) are actually implemented; the visible help and implemented commands diverge. (3) Note that the script will create and write logs under ~/.local/share/certcheck and may record arbitrary inputs (including secrets) to history.log and other .log files—clean up or change the data directory only after confirming the script honors CERTCHECK_DIR (it currently ignores it). (4) If you plan to run it, do so first in an isolated environment (VM or container) and search the full script for any external endpoints or credential access. If you cannot audit the full script, treat the skill as untrusted.
llm.findings: [no-findings] unexpected: Static pre-scan reported no findings. That doesn't imply safety: the primary concerns come from mismatches between SKILL.md and the included script and from local file writes. Also the provided script was truncated in the bundle preview, so network-related behavior later in the file may not have been visible here.
